title: AEOeye vs Evertune: One-Off AI Audit or Always-On GEO Platform?
metaTitle: AEOeye vs Evertune: Which Should You Use? (2026)
metaDescription: AEOeye vs Evertune: a one-off AI visibility audit (free, then $29) against a demo-led GEO platform listed at $800 a month. Who should pick which, and why.
shortAnswer: Pick AEOeye if you want a one-time answer to "does AI name us, and who does it name instead?": a free ChatGPT check, or a $29 report across five engines. Pick Evertune if AI visibility is a funded channel and you need always-on, repeatedly sampled tracking plus content and advertising tools. Its Pro plan is listed at $800 a month (as of October 2026), sold through a demo.
intro:
This comparison is based on Evertune's public documentation (its pricing, platform, methodology and FAQ pages, read on 3 October 2026), and we have not tested Evertune hands-on. AEOeye is our product, so we say plainly where Evertune is stronger.

We left out two claims that circulate in older write-ups: a roughly $3,000-a-month floor and a US-only panel. We could not verify either from Evertune's own pages, which list a Pro plan at $800 a month and "global language and country tracking". For the price detail, see [how much Evertune costs](/answers/how-much-does-evertune-cost).

sections.heading: Which should you choose, AEOeye or Evertune?
sections.body:
Choose by the question you need answered. AEOeye answers a one-off question: does AI name my brand, and who does it name instead? Evertune is a continuous measurement and activation platform for teams that will act on its data every week.

- **Pick AEOeye** if you have never checked what ChatGPT says about you. Start with the [free audit](/), then add the $29 report when you want Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity too.
- **Pick Evertune** if AI visibility is already a funded channel. You need weekly or daily tracking across many models, content production and advertising in one place, and you can run a sales-led onboarding at $800 a month or more.
- **Pick neither** if you want continuous tracking at a lower price. Self-serve trackers cost far less; see [Evertune alternatives](/alternatives/evertune).

Our view: run a one-time audit before you buy any monitoring platform. A tracker measures change, and you cannot judge a trend until you know whether you have a problem at all.

sections.heading: What is each tool actually built for?
sections.body:
AEOeye is an audit: you ask, it answers, you act. Evertune is a platform that measures, then helps you act and advertise. They overlap on one question (is my brand named?) and differ on everything after it.

**AEOeye.** The free audit gives an AI visibility score and grade, three unbranded buyer questions asked to ChatGPT live with the real answers shown in full, the competitors AI recommends instead, and starter fixes. The $29 one-time report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity, ten questions instead of three, a five-layer SEO foundation audit and a fix roadmap emailed as a PDF. Each engine is tested at the default tier a free user would get. There is no subscription.

**Evertune.** Its [homepage](https://www.evertune.ai/) describes four steps: Explore (what buyers ask AI), Measure (where you stand against competitors across 11 models), Act (content and website fixes) and Advertise (ChatGPT ads and retargeting). Its [company page](https://www.evertune.ai/about-us/company-overview) says it was founded in 2024 by early Trade Desk team members and lists Halo Collar, Canada Goose, HexClad, Roku and WPP as clients.

![Business meeting where a team studies data on a presentation screen](https://images.pexels.com/photos/5716030/pexels-photo-5716030.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How do AEOeye and Evertune compare side by side?
sections.body:
The biggest differences are price basis, how often you measure, and what happens after measurement. AEOeye charges per report; Evertune charges per month and sells through a demo. The table after these sections lists every row, and four deserve a note.

- **Price basis.** AEOeye costs $0 for the free audit and $29 one-time. Evertune's [pricing page](https://www.evertune.ai/pricing) lists Pro at $800 a month and Enterprise as custom, with no billing terms. At list price, a year of Pro is $9,600 (our arithmetic).
- **Prompt limits.** Pro lists 100,000 prompts tracked across 11 AI models. The page does not say whether that counts prompts or sampled responses, so ask in the demo, because the method asks each prompt up to 100 times.
- **Engines.** Evertune's [FAQ](https://www.evertune.ai/resources/faq) lists ChatGPT, ChatGPT Search, Gemini, Gemini Search, AI Mode, AI Overviews, Meta AI, Claude, Copilot, Perplexity and DeepSeek. AEOeye covers five engines in the $29 report and ChatGPT alone in the free audit.
- **Access.** Both Evertune plans end in "Request a demo", and we found no free tier or trial on that page. AEOeye starts at the homepage.

sections.heading: Where is Evertune stronger than AEOeye?
sections.body:
Evertune is stronger on measurement depth, prompt sourcing and what you can do after measuring. That is a different class of product, not a bigger version of ours.

**Repeated sampling.** Evertune asks each prompt up to 100 times per model. That matters: [OpenAI's documentation](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/reproducible_outputs_with_the_seed_parameter) says its API outputs are non-deterministic by default, and [SparkToro's study](https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/) of 2,961 runs found under a 1-in-100 chance of getting the same brand list twice and advised asking at least 60 to 100 times. One answer is a draw, not a rate.

We checked Evertune's margins against the [standard formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margin_of_error): 100 responses at a 50% mention rate give about ±10 points at 95% confidence, which matches its [methodology page](https://www.evertune.ai/platform/methodology). The study is Evertune's own (running shoes, July 2026) and covers sampling noise only, not whether the prompts are well chosen.

**Prompts from real users.** Evertune builds prompt sets from EverPanel, which it describes as over 150 million real conversations. It also reports what a model knows from training (direct API access) separately from what the consumer app says after a live search, and reads the gap as a diagnosis.

**Action.** Its [platform pages](https://www.evertune.ai/platform/act) cover Site Audit, Content Studio drafts and affiliate placements, and its FAQ says Site Audit crawls up to 1,000 pages. The pricing page does not make clear which plan includes which tool. Forrester listed Evertune as a notable vendor in its Q3 2026 AEO landscape, [per Evertune's own post](https://www.evertune.ai/resources/insights-on-ai/evertune-named-a-notable-vendor-in-forresters-answer-engine-optimization-technologies-landscape-q3-2026).

One caution: its AI Brand Score weights position, with first place at 100% and second at 90%. SparkToro put the chance of the same list in the same order below 1 in 1,000. Averaging 100 samples helps, but we would read the Visibility Score, the share of responses naming you, first.

sections.heading: Where is AEOeye stronger than Evertune?
sections.body:
AEOeye is stronger on cost, speed and readability for a first answer. You get the real engine answers without a demo or a monthly commitment, and you can judge them yourself.

- **Cost and commitment.** $0, then $29 once, against a demo-led platform at $800 a month or more.
- **Evidence you can read.** You see the full answers and the competitors AI names instead, not an index you must trust.
- **Realistic tiers.** Each engine is tested at the default tier a free user would get, so you see what most buyers see.
- **No data science needed.** The output is a list of fixes, not a dashboard to interpret.

The limits are real. The audit reports the answers returned when we asked; it gives no visibility rate with a margin of error. AEOeye is not a daily tracker, does not write your content and cannot guarantee a recommendation. For ongoing monitoring across hundreds of prompts, dedicated trackers do that job; see the [best AI visibility tools](/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools).

![Detailed business stages displayed onscreen, useful for planning and strategy sessions](https://images.pexels.com/photos/7948041/pexels-photo-7948041.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: Does Evertune block AI crawlers on its own site?
sections.body:
No. In AEOeye's crawler access study (one fetch per site on 3 October 2026), Evertune's robots.txt blocks no AI crawler: it disallows only /legal/ and /404. The site serves an llms.txt file, and its homepage has server-rendered JSON-LD of type Organization, WebSite, SearchAction and EntryPoint.

That is a neutral fact, not a verdict on the product. None of the 43 AI-visibility vendors in the study blocked an AI bot, so it is the norm. The [study hub](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory) has the method and per-site data.

keyTakeaways: AEOeye is a one-off audit (free on ChatGPT, $29 for five engines); Evertune is a demo-led platform with Pro listed at $800 a month as of October 2026.
Evertune's 100-sample method is a real strength: single AI answers vary, and its published margins match the standard formula.
Evertune adds site audit, content drafting and advertising; AEOeye does not track daily, write content or run ads.
Run a one-time audit first, then buy continuous tracking once you know what you are tracking.

faqs.q: Is AEOeye a replacement for Evertune?
faqs.a: No. AEOeye is a one-time audit that shows what ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity say about your brand today. Evertune is a continuous platform with repeated sampling, content tools and advertising. Most teams could use the audit first, then decide whether a monitoring platform is worth its monthly cost.

As of October 2026, Evertune's pricing page lists Pro at $800 a month and Enterprise as custom, with no billing terms stated. Both plans lead to a demo request. A year of Pro at list price is $9,600. Confirm contract length and what the 100,000-prompt allowance counts in the demo.

faqs.q: Does Evertune have a free trial?
faqs.a: We found no free tier or trial on Evertune's pricing page, where both plans end in "Request a demo", and its get-started page asks for a demo form. That reflects public documentation read on 3 October 2026, not hands-on use, so ask Evertune directly if a trial matters to you.

faqs.q: Why does Evertune sample each prompt 100 times?
faqs.a: AI answers differ from run to run, so one response is a single draw. Evertune asks each prompt up to 100 times per model to estimate a mention rate with a small margin of error. An independent SparkToro study similarly advised asking at least 60 to 100 times and averaging.

faqs.q: Can I start with AEOeye and move to Evertune later?
faqs.a: Yes, and we think that order is sensible. The free audit shows whether AI names you and who it names instead. If that gap is worth tracking weekly, a platform like Evertune, or a cheaper tracker, can measure whether your fixes move the number.
